title: Zooming out to see where you are, in the held world
question: You are walking in the held world and pull the camera back to see where you are. Which of these three is the picture you want?
context_md:
The held world (`--bin druid`), one moment, one spot, the camera pulled back three different ways. Same world, same centre cell, and **all three drawn at the same size on screen** — the size a maximised window gives.

Two of them frame the land identically and differ only in how much of it survives; the third frames it differently. Each pane's own numbers are underneath it.

**Measured already, so you do not have to judge it.** The zoom ladder has four rungs, and the third of them is the only one that cannot spend the extra pixels the sandbox and the lab now default to — walking outwards you get sharp, sharp, *soft*, sharp. Your answer decides between leaving that alone, dropping the soft rung off the ladder, and changing the engine so it can be sharp too. **Judge the pictures; the engineering is priced either way.**

One caveat that is mine rather than the engine's: to put all three at one size, one of the sharp panes had to be stretched by a third (every third row and column doubled). Nothing was thrown away and no pane was softened to match another.

items.label: rung 3 as it ships today — soft

meta.of the whole world: 60% of its width, all of its height
meta.black border: none — the land fills the screen

items.label: rung 4, the next rung out — sharp, already possible

meta.of the whole world: 80% of its width, all of its height
meta.black border: 25% of the screen, above and below the land

items.label: rung 3 made sharp — needs the engine change

meta.of the whole world: 60% of its width, all of its height
meta.black border: none — the land fills the screen
